sources.title: A Containerized Microservice Architecture for a ROS 2 Autonomous Driving Software: An End-to-End Latency Evaluation
sources.role: Author paper/preprint used to verify the reported architecture, method/evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors present a containerized microservice architecture for a real-world ROS 2 autonomous-driving application, using containers to isolate services on a common compute platform.
claims.context: Architecture description verified from the author abstract.

claims.text: The authors report lower mean end-to-end latency and significantly reduced maximum latency for the presented containerized microservice deployment compared with their standard bare-Linux deployment.
claims.context: Abstract-level result; detailed workload and statistical setup were not inspected in this verification pass.

metrics.name: reported mean end-to-end latency improvement
metrics.context: Author-reported range for the presented microservice architecture versus standard bare-Linux deployment; detailed experiment conditions remain unresolved.

limitations.text: This pass verified the primary abstract but did not reconstruct the full hardware/software setup, workload, jitter distributions, CPU/memory results, or statistical treatment.
The reported latency result is tied to the paper's presented autonomous-driving application and must not be generalized to containerization in all automotive workloads.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for A Containerized Microservice Architecture for a ROS 2 Autonomous Driving Software: An End-to-End Latency Evaluation; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary abstract verifies the containerized ROS 2 microservice architecture and the reported 5-8% mean end-to-end latency improvement, but the complete evaluation setup and limitations require full-paper inspection.

unresolved_questions: Inspect the full paper to verify hardware, ROS 2 topology, container/runtime configuration, jitter and resource-utilization measurements, statistical treatment, and explicit limitations.

editorial.why_now_note: Container consolidation on common compute is directly relevant to centralized SDV runtime architecture, but abstract-only evaluation evidence is insufficient for final comparison.
editorial.rationale: Keep as an evidence lead; do not promote the 5-8% figure into the report until its full experimental context is verified.
